mechanism_fidelity.rationale: Overlapping routes provide endpoint observations that constrain hidden service-delay changes. Comparing measured differences with additive-model predictions and adjusting compatible maps preserves the inverse-modeling chain. Non-uniqueness, sparse coverage, measurement error and model limits remain explicit.

target_fidelity.rationale: Old/new comparisons at fixed low load isolate the cache-policy flag within replay because it is the only configuration difference. This provides bounded evidence distinguishing a deployment effect from load-only variation, without claiming complete attribution of the live regression or identifying a code mechanism.

operational_coherence.rationale: Independent calibration establishes the additive model, stable route membership and bounded endpoint error. The proposed measurements therefore constrain service-delay changes operationally. Six initial endpoint trials and two follow-up trials fit the ledger; fitting and held-out assessment fit two analysis passes. No later inspection is needed to support the stated bounded inference.

validity.rationale: The mapping preserves model-based inference from overlapping paths and supplies a controlled deployment contrast relevant to attribution. Its conclusions remain explicitly limited to measured replay constraints.

uncertainty: Replay results are not supplied, so the direction, magnitude and localization of any deployment effect remain unknown.
The non-unique solution set from r1-r3 may permit broad r4 predictions, limiting the discriminatory strength of the held-out residual check.
Low-load replay does not establish deployment effects at high load or their contribution to the full live regression; candidate explanations may also be incomplete.
